questions.question: The solidified lava of a volcano belongs to which rock family?
questions.solution:
Option 1 is correct, i.e. __Igneous Rock__.

__
 
• Igneous rock is one of three main types of rock; the others are sedimentary and metamorphic.
 
• Igneous__ is formed by the magma or lava refrigeration and solidification.

Extra facts:

 
• Metamorphic rocks are rocks that have changed as they form due to intense heat or pressure.
 
• Sedimentary rocks are rock forms that are formed by aggregation or deposition of small particles and subsequent cementation of mineral or organic particles on the surface of the Earth's ocean floor or other water bodies.

questions.question: Which article supplements 11th fundamental duty of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Article 21A.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 21 A was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002: **This article declares that the State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years in such a manner as the State may determine.**
 
• Article 51 A was added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976.
 
 
• **This article specifies a code of 11 Fundamental Duties.**
 
• Originally, article 51 A contained 10 Fundamental Duties.
 
• **The fundamental duty to provide opportunities for education to his child or ward between the age of 6-14 years was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002 as the 11th **fundamental duty**. **
 
 
 
• **So from the content of Article 21A and 11th fundamental duty**, we can conclude that Article 21A supplements the 11th fundamental duty of the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Article 45**- To provide **early childhood care and education** for all children until they complete the **age of six years**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Article 31 B was added by the **1st Constitutional Amendment Act of 1951.**

 
 
• This article was introduced to **protect the laws mentioned under the Ninth schedule from judicial scrutiny** on the **ground of violation of Fundamental Rights.**
 
• In 2007, the Supreme Court ruled that the laws included in the Ninth schedule after 24 April 1973 are now **open to judicial review.**
 
 
 
• Article 243 G was added by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992: It specifies powers, authority and responsibilities of Panchayats.

questions.question: A person appointed as a judge of the Supreme Court, before entering upon his Office, has to make and subscribe an oath or affirmation before

options.text: President, or some person appointed by him

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President or some person appointed by him**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

**Oath or Affirmation**

__
 
• A person appointed as a judge of the Supreme Court, before entering upon his office, has to make and subscribe an oath or affirmation before **the President, or some person appointed by him for this purpose**. **Hence, option 2 is correct.**
 
• **In his oath, a judge of the Supreme Court swears:**
 
 
• to bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India;
 
• to uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India;
 
• to duly and faithfully and to the best of his ability, knowledge and judgement perform the duties of the Office without fear or favour, affection or ill-will; and
 
• to uphold the Constitution and the laws.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Qualifications of Judges**

 
• A person to be appointed as a judge of the Supreme Court should have the following qualifications:
 
 
• He should be a citizen of India.
 
• He should have been a judge of a High Court (or high courts in succession) for five years; or
 
• He should have been an advocate of a High Court (or High Courts in succession) for ten years; or
 
• He should be a distinguished jurist in the opinion of the president.
 
 

**From the above, it is clear that the Constitution has not prescribed minimum age for appointment as a judge of the Supreme Court.**

questions.question: How many members are there in Finance Commission of India, EXCEPT the Chairman?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Four**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Finance Commission of India is constituted by the President of India every five years.
 
• The Commission consists of a Chairman and four other members, thus excluding the Chairman, there are four members.
 
• These members are appointed by the President based on their expertise in public affairs and economics.
 
• The primary function of the Finance Commission is to recommend measures and methods on how revenues need to be distributed between the Centre and the States.
 
• The recommendations made by the Finance Commission are advisory in nature and not binding on the government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Provision:**

 
 
• The Finance Commission is established under Article 280 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Its role is to define the financial relations between the central government and the individual state governments.
 
 
 
• **Terms of Reference:**
 
 
• The President provides the terms of reference for each Finance Commission.
 
• These terms outline the specific issues the Commission should address in its report.
 
 
 
• **Notable Recommendations:**
 
 
• Recommendations on the distribution of net proceeds of taxes to be shared between the Centre and the States.
 
• Principles that should govern the grants-in-aid to the states by the Centre.
 
 
 
• **Advisory Role:**
 
 
• The Finance Commission's recommendations are advisory, meaning the government can choose to implement or not implement them.
 
• Despite this, the recommendations carry significant weight and are usually respected.

questions.question: Which of the following sites of Indus valley civilization is not on the bank of river Indus ?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is - __Ropar__**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Ropar__**

 __
 
• Located in present-day Punjab on the banks of the **Sutlej River__**, not the Indus.
 
• Excavated by **__Y.D. Sharma__**; one of the few Harappan sites in the easternmost region.
 
• Shows evidence of **__Harappan to post-Harappan cultural sequence__**.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__ **

__
 
• **Mohenjodaro__**

 __
 
• Situated on the **right bank of the Indus River__**.
 
• Known for the **__Great Bath__** and advanced drainage system.
 
 
 
• **__Chanhudaro__**
 __
 
• Located in Sindh, near the **Indus basin__**.
 
• Famous as a centre for **__bead making__**.
 
 
 
• **__Kot Diji__**
 __
 
• Situated on the **left bank of the Indus__** in Sindh.
 
• Represents the **__Kot Diji pre-Harappan phase__** preceding mature Harappan culture.

questions.question: Which one of the following is not among the Four Noble Truths of Lord Buddha?

options.text: The world is the home of sorrows
Desire is the cause of suffering
If desires are not relieved, then misery can be avoided
This can be done by following the eight fold path

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**If desires are not relieved, then misery can be avoided**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Four Noble Truths comprise the essence of Buddha's teachings, though they leave much left unexplained.
 
• They are the **truth of suffering (dukkha), the truth of the cause of suffering (samudaya), the truth of the end of suffering (nirhodha), and the truth of the path that leads to the end of suffering (magga)​.**
 
• If desires are not relieved, then misery can be avoided is not among the Four Noble Truths of Lord Buddha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Buddhism** is a widespread Asian religion or philosophical tradition based on a series of original teachings attributed to Gautama Buddha.

 
 
• It originated in ancient India as a Sramana tradition sometime between the 6th and 4th centuries BCE, spreading through much of Asia.
 
 
 
• The **Eightfold Path** consists of eight practices:** right view, right resolve, right speech, right conduct, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right samadhi ('meditative absorption or union').**
 
• The Noble Eightfold Path is one of the principal teachings of Buddhism, taught to lead to Arhatship.

questions.question: In the year ________, the Maratha Empire ceased to exist with the surrender of the Marathas to the British, ending the Third Anglo-Maratha War.
questions.solution:
__
 
• **The Third Anglo-Maratha War ended in 1818 with the surrender of the Marathas to the British.**__
 
• The Third Anglo-Maratha War took place in Maharashtra and its neighboring areas in 1817 and 1818.
 
• The main reason for the Third Anglo-Maratha war was British conflict with the **Pindaris** whom the British suspected were being protected by the Marathas.
 
• The** Treaty of Mandasor** was signed between the British and the Holkar chief in 1818.
 
• Main reasons for the loss of Marathas were lack of unity among the Maratha chiefs themselves, lack of good relations with other Indian princes and ruling dynasties and failure to understand the British political and diplomatic strengths.

questions.question: _______ Five Year Plan was based on the ‘Harrod-Domar Model'.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**First -Five Year Plan.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The First Five Year Plan of India was based on the Harrod Domar Model.
 
• First Five-Year Plan of India:
 
 
• It was launched for the duration of 1951 to 1956, under the leadership of Jawaharlal Nehru.
 
• It was based on the Harrod-Domar model with a few modifications.
 
• Its main focus was on the agricultural development of the country.
 
• This plan was successful and achieved a growth rate of 3.6% (more than its target of 2.1%). 
 
• At the end of this plan, five IITs were set up in the country.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 
Second Five-Year Plan (1956‑61):

 
 
• This plan was based on the P.C. Mahalanobis Model.
 
• In this plan, heavy industries and minerals were on top priority and 20.1% of the total outlay was allocated for this sector.
 
• The plan was also successful and it achieved a 4.1% rate of growth.
 
• Various important large industries like Steel Plant at Durgapur, Bhilai and Rourkela were established during this plan.
 
 
 
• 
 
Third Five-Year Plan (1961-66):

 
 
• This plan is also called “*Gadgil Yojana*.”
 
• This plan could not achieve its aim of a 5.6% growth rate.
 
 
 
• 
 
Fifth Five Year Plan: 

 
 
• The period of the fifth five-year plan was 1974 to 1978.
 
• The Draft of the fifth plan was prepared and launched by D.P. Dhar in the backdrop of economic crisis arising out of run-away inflation fuelled by a hike in oil prices and failure of the Government takeover of the wholesale trade in wheat.
 
• The targeted growth rate was 4.4% but the actual growth achieved was 4.8%.

questions.question: Which type of seeds played an important role in Green Revolution in India?

__
 
• The Green Revolution started in 1965 with the first introduction of High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds in Indian agriculture.
 
• In 1965, the government with the help of Indian geneticists M.S. Swaminathan, known as the father of the Green Revolution, launched the Green Revolution.
 
 
• The movement lasted from 1967 to 1978 and was a great success.
 
 
 
• This was coupled with better and efficient irrigation and the correct use of fertilizers to boost the crop.
 
 
• The result of the Green Revolution was to make India self-sufficient when it came to food grains.
 
 
 
• These HYV seeds had more success with the wheat crop and were highly effective in regions that had proper irrigation.

questions.question: The direction of acceleration in uniform circular motion is along the

options.text: tangent to the circle at the point of observation

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**direction perpendicular to the velocity.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **​**__The direction of the acceleration is** inwards. **The acceleration in a uniform circular motion is along the radius and towards the center.
 
• The** movement** of a **body** following a **circular path** is called a** circular motion.**
 
• The **motion** of a** body moving with constant speed** along a **circular path** is called **Uniform Circular Motion.**
 
• In this motion **speed **is **constant** but the **velocity changes**.
 
• In the case of uniform circular motion, the acceleration is **aᵣ = v²/r = ω²r.**
 
• A **particle** is **moving **in a **uniform circular motion:**
 __
 
• **​**Velocity is changing at every instant.
 
• There is no tangential acceleration.
 
• Its speed is constant.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3ef378d205cbfb27e26e99bab78fc7f1ff9518b1b6b7887b98bd4416e7b7cbab.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Examples for Circular Motion:**

 
 
• **​**The motion of blades of the windmills.
 
• The tip of the second hand of a watch with a circular dial shows uniform circular motion.
 
• The motion of electrons around its nucleus.

questions.question: Who among the following Sultans of Delhi started the system of Sijda and Paibos?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ghiyas ud din Balban.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ** The correct answer is option 3, i.e. Ghiyas ud din Balban, who was the ninth Sultan of Delhi and ruled from 1266 to 1287 AD.**
 
• ** Sijda and Paibos were two forms of obeisance** that were introduced by Balban to establish his authority and enhance the status of the Sultanate in the eyes of the people.
 
• Sijda involved prostratin**g oneself before the Sultan** and touching his feet as a sign of submission and respect. P**aibos, on the other hand, required the person to kneel before the Sultan and kiss his feet.**
 
• Balban's strict enforcement of these customs was meant to reinforce the idea of the** Sultan as a divine ruler **and to discourage any challenges to his authority.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Nasir u din Muhammad was the third Sultan of the Khilji dynasty and is known for his patronage of scholars and poets.
 
• **Qutb ud-Din Aibak was the founder of the Slave dynasty and the first Muslim ruler of Delhi**.
 
• He is known for his military conquests and his construction of the Qutub Minar.

questions.question: Non-metals are generally bad conductors of electricity. However, graphite is a good conductor of electricity because it
questions.solution:
The correct answer __**has free electrons**____**.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Graphite:

 
 
• Graphite is a form of carbon that has a hexagonal lattice structure.
 
• It is made up of layers of carbon atoms that are bonded together in an sp2 hybridization.
 
• The layers are held together by weak Van der Waals forces, which allow them to slide over each other easily.
 
• Graphite is a good conductor of electricity and has a high melting point.
 
• It is used in applications such as electrodes, lubricants, and pencils.
 
• **Graphite can conduct electricity because of the delocalized (free) electrons in its structure.**
 
• These arise because each carbon atom is only bonded to 3 other carbon atoms.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The property of an element that exists in more than one physical form is called allotropy and the forms are termed allotropes
 
• Carbon shows allotropy due to catenation, which is the linking of atoms of the same element with one another to form long chains.
 
• There are various allotropes of carbon__ that exist in nature including __diamond__, __graphene__, and __fullerenes.__

questions.question: What is the cell wall of a plant made of ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cellulose**__.

__
 
• Plant cell walls are primarily made of cellulose.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Cellulose is the most abundant macromolecule on Earth.
 
 
• Cellulose fibers are long, linear polymers of hundreds of glucose molecules.
 
• These fibres aggregate into bundles of about 40, which are called microfibrils.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Carbohydrates are the sugars, starches, and fibres found in fruits, grains, vegetables, and milk products.
 
 
• A carbohydrate is a biomolecule consisting of carbon (C), hydrogen (H), and oxygen (O) atoms.
 
 
 
• Lipids are molecules that contain hydrocarbons and make up the building blocks of the structure and function of living cells.
 
 
• A lipid is a biomolecule that is soluble in nonpolar solvents.
 
 
 
• A lipoprotein is a biochemical assembly whose primary function is to transport hydrophobic lipid also known as fat molecules in water, as in blood plasma or other extracellular fluids.
 
 
• It consists of a Triglyceride and Cholesterol centre, surrounded by a phospholipid outer shell, with the hydrophilic portions oriented outward towards the surrounding water and lipophilic portions oriented inward toward the lipid centre.
